title: Senior Signal Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-255Z. MOS 255Z—Senior Signal Warrant Officer
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. DOD 8570.01M Baseline Technical certification IAT
Level III or IAM Level II requirements.
    b. Prerequisites. Demonstrated proficiency in MOS 255A, 255N or 255S.
    c. MOS 255Z. MOS 255Z is a non-accession MOS. It is the capstone MOS for 255A, 255N,
and 255S at the executive level (CW5) for cyberspace information technology and cybersecurity
activities. They serve as senior technical and tactical advisors for Department of Defense
Information Networks (DODIN) operations at any echelon of command.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. Refer to table 6-6 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all warrant
officer MOS.
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) Physical Demands Category – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) WO1/CW2/CW3 and CW4 does not apply
         (3) CW5 must--
               (a) Meet qualifications listed for one of the feeder MOSs 255A, 255N, or 255S.
               (b) Successfully perform at the CW4 level as described in the duties paragraph for
the feeder MOSs.
               (c) Be a U.S. citizen.
               (d) Possess a security clearance of TOP SECRET with special compartmentalized
information (SCI) access.
              (e) Minimum OPAT scores for physical demands category moderate (gold) are: Long
Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs.,
and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles
              (f) Meet vision and hearing standards of AR 40-501 for assignment of officers to
Signal Corps, normal color discrimination per AR 40-501, and have full use of both hands.
              (g) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE)
course no later than 1 year after promotion to CW5 except Reserve Component.
              (h) DoD 8570.01-M CSSP Manager and IASAE Level III certifications are desired.
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2/CW3/CW4 does not apply.
         (2) CW5--
               (a) Provides technical guidance and expertise regarding operations and policies for
information systems requirements, cybersecurity operations, network administration, and signal
maintenance to support and enable mission command.
               (b) Contributes to the MOS life cycle management for all personnel proponent
functions to include the assignment process and oversee personnel management matters
pertaining to Signal Branch.
               (c) Coordinates and provides oversight for information technology contracting,
procurement, and materiel acquisition programs.
               (d) Develops policy recommendations and provide technical guidance and advice to
commanders and staffs on the management and operation of cyberspace information technology
data networks, systems, services, and cybersecurity activities of Army, Joint, intergovernmental,
interagency, and multinational organizations.
               (e) May serve as senior technical and tactical advisors for the Department of
Defense Information Network (DODIN) operation at any echelon of command.
               (f) May serve as the Senior Signal Warrant Officer for Theater Tactical Signal
Brigade or Corps G6 staff.
               (g) May serve as Career Program Manager or Technical Director for U.S. Army
Signal School.
               (h) May serve as Command Chief Warrant Officer for JCSE, WHCA, Theater Signal
Commands, Senior Technical Advisor for ASCC, or ACOM G6 Staff.
              (i) May serve as Regimental Chief Warrant Officer for U.S. Army Signal Regiment.
              (j) May serve as Command Chief Warrant Officer for U.S. Army Network Enterprise
Technology Command.
              (k) May serve as Senior Signal Technical Advisor for DISA, COCOM, Joint J6 Staff,
intergovernmental, interagency, or multinational partners.
              (l) May serve as Chief Technology Officer for HQDA G6/CIO Staff.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
        (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
        (2) Table 8-255S-1. Physical requirements.
        (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of three definable skill levels:
W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-255Z-1. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-255Z-2. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
